name: str_ends
title: Detect a match at the end of a string

origin.description: Return TRUE where string ends with pattern. This is str_detect restricted to the end of each string.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern the string must end with. A plain character vector is a regular expression, wrapped as (pattern)$. fixed and coll compare the end literally or by collation. The empty string and boundary patterns are not allowed.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If TRUE, invert the logical result. Must be a single TRUE or FALSE.

origin.details: A regular expression is pasted into (pattern)$ and passed to stri_detect_regex with the pattern's regex options. fixed and coll call stri_endswith_fixed and stri_endswith_coll. Recycling, missing values, and names follow str_detect.
origin.example:
fruit <- c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple")
result <- str_ends(fruit, "e")
writeLines(paste0('str_ends(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "e") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.'))

translation.description: Return true where string ends with pattern.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list is wrapped as (pattern)$ and searched as a regular expression. fixed and coll use the stringi end matchers. The empty string and boundary are errors.

arguments.name: negate
arguments.text: If true, invert each real match. Must be True or False.

translation.details: The grouped anchor keeps a|b inside the end test. Options come from pattern_opts. A missing pattern element is pasted as the letters NA, giving (NA)$. Names and recycling follow str_detect.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.detect import str_ends
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
result = str_ends(fruit, "e")
words = ", ".join("TRUE" if item else "FALSE" for item in result)
print('str_ends(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "e") returns ' + words + '.')
